name: Glute Bridge March
description: An isometric and dynamic glute challenge performed by holding a glute bridge position while alternately lifting each foot off the floor in a marching pattern. The alternating leg lift forces the planted glute and core to resist pelvic rotation and maintain a stable bridge, increasing unilateral demand without additional load.

execution.starting_position: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart. Drive the hips up into a glute bridge position.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Optionally place a resistance band loop just above the knees for additional challenge.
steps: Step 1: Lift the hips into a glute bridge and hold the position, squeezing both glutes.
Step 2: Keeping the hips level, lift one foot off the floor and bring the knee toward the chest.
Step 3: Hold for a moment, then return the foot to the floor.
Step 4: Repeat on the opposite side while maintaining the bridge position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe steadily throughout. Do not hold your breath.
common_mistakes: Allowing the hips to drop or rotate when lifting each foot
Pushing through the lower back rather than the glutes
safety_considerations: Ensure the hips stay level — place a dumbbell on the hips as a feedback tool if needed
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Hips fully extended throughout. Each knee lifts to approximately 90 degrees.
coaching_cues: Squeeze both glutes even when one leg is marching
